- Build a complete, playable 2D car racing game app.

## Requirements
- Do not ask clarifying questions; make reasonable assumptions.
- Save small JPEG screenshots for checks, viewport at most 1280px wide, and read only the latest screenshot.

## Decisions
- Built a self-contained browser game with an arcade-style night-racing theme, keyboard controls, AI opponents, lap tracking, boost, pause, and replay.

## Work State
### Completed
- Created the game interface and styling in `index.html` and `style.css`.
- Implemented racing gameplay and rendering in `game.js`.
- Checked JavaScript syntax with `node --check game.js`.
- Opened the app in Playwright and captured/inspected a latest JPEG screenshot.

### Active

- (none)

## Next Move
1. Optionally perform a more complete gameplay check; no further changes are currently pending.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game UI and controls.
- `style.css`: Responsive visual design.
- `game.js`: Canvas track, cars, AI, controls, race state and HUD.
- `screenshots/apex-latest.jpg`: Latest inspected screenshot.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- The development server was started with `python3 -m http.server 3002`.
- Playwright initially reported missing Chromium; `playwright-cli install-browser chromium` resolved it.
- A 404 for `/favicon.ico` appeared during initial browser load.

content.text:
Built the playable APEX / Night Run racing game in `index.html`, `style.css`, and `game.js`.

It includes keyboard driving, boost, AI opponents, lap and position tracking, pause/resume, replay, and a responsive race interface. Checked JavaScript syntax and inspected the latest browser screenshot at `screenshots/apex-latest.jpg`.

Assumption: I treated the request as a self-contained browser game, with no external game engine. Start it with `python3 -m http.server 3002` and open `http://localhost:3002`.
